description: Pushkar, Sonepur, Kumbh, Hornbill, Surajkund, regional matching

questions.stem: The Pushkar Camel Fair, one of India's largest livestock fairs, is held annually in:
questions.explanation: Pushkar Mela — held in November on Kartik Purnima (full moon of the Hindu month Kartik) at Pushkar, Ajmer district, Rajasthan. Pushkar Lake is associated with the only major Brahma temple in India. ~50,000 camels traded; competitions for moustaches, turbans, balloon races, and a sacred dip on the final day. Other Rajasthan fairs — Marwar (Jodhpur), Nagaur Cattle Fair, Teej, Gangaur. International tourism — over a million visitors annually.

questions.stem: Sonepur Mela — described as Asia's largest cattle fair — is held in:

options.option_text: Bihar (Saran district, at the confluence of Ganga and Gandak)

questions.explanation: Sonepur Cattle Fair (Sonepur Mela / Harihar Kshetra Mela) — historically the largest cattle fair in Asia, held on Kartik Purnima at Sonepur on the Sonepur-Hajipur stretch where the Gandak meets the Ganga. Mentioned in Mughal records — Aurangzeb's reign saw the fair flourish. The Harihar Nath temple is nearby. Animals traded — elephants, horses, camels, buffaloes, cattle (the elephant trade has dwindled post-1972 Wildlife Protection Act).

questions.stem: The 'Hornbill Festival' — a tribal cultural fair held every December — is the signature festival of:
questions.explanation: Hornbill Festival — held 1-10 December every year at Naga Heritage Village, Kisama (10 km from Kohima). Showcases all 17 major Naga tribes — Angami, Ao, Chakhesang, Chang, Khiamniungan, Konyak, Kuki, Lotha, Phom, Pochury, Rengma, Sangtam, Sumi, Yimchunger, Zeliang, Pochury, Pochuri. Named after the great hornbill — important in Naga folklore. Aligned with Nagaland's statehood day (1 Dec 1963). Often called the 'Festival of Festivals'.

questions.stem: The Surajkund International Crafts Mela — showcasing handicrafts from across India and abroad — is held annually in:
questions.explanation: Surajkund Mela — held every February since 1987 at Surajkund near Faridabad, Haryana. Organised by Haryana Tourism, Union Ministries of Tourism, Textiles, Culture, External Affairs. Features one 'partner state' of India and one 'theme country' annually. Surajkund (literally 'Lake of the Sun') is a 10th-century reservoir built by Tomar king Surajpal. Got 'international' tag in 2010. Other major craft fairs — Dilli Haat, Shilparamam (Hyderabad), Kala Ghoda Festival (Mumbai).

questions.stem: The Kumbh Mela rotates between four cities. Which of the following is NOT a Kumbh Mela site?
questions.explanation: Four Kumbh sites — Prayagraj (Triveni Sangam, U.P.), Haridwar (Ganga, Uttarakhand), Ujjain (Shipra, M.P.), Nashik (Godavari, Maharashtra). Mathura is NOT a Kumbh site. UNESCO inscribed Kumbh Mela on Intangible Cultural Heritage list (2017). Kumbh occurs at each site every 12 years; an 'Ardha (half) Kumbh' falls in between at Prayagraj and Haridwar (~6-year gap). Maha Kumbh 2025 at Prayagraj — one of the largest gatherings of humans ever (estimated >40 crore visitors over 45 days).

questions.stem: Match fair with state — which pairing is INCORRECT?
questions.explanation: Hemis Festival is in Ladakh — celebrated at Hemis Monastery to commemorate Padmasambhava (Guru Rinpoche). Held on 10th day of Tibetan lunar calendar's 5th month (June-July). Famous for masked Cham dances. Punjab's notable festivals — Lohri, Vaisakhi, Hola Mohalla (Anandpur Sahib). Tarnetar Fair (Gujarat, Surendranagar) — famous for tribal swayamvar. Goa Carnival — Christian/Portuguese-origin festival before Lent (Feb-Mar). Pongal — Tamil harvest festival in mid-January.

questions.stem: The 'Rann Utsav' — a tourist festival featuring tents, folk music and dance — is held in the white desert of:
questions.explanation: Rann Utsav — held November-February at Dhordo, Kutch district, Gujarat — across the white salt marsh of the Rann of Kutch. Tent City accommodates thousands of tourists. Started 2005; rapidly became a flagship of Gujarat tourism. UNWTO recognised Dhordo as 'Best Tourism Village 2023'. Highlights — full-moon nights on the salt flats, Bhuj-style cuisine, Kutchi embroidery shopping, camel safaris. Distinct from the Pushkar Camel Fair (Rajasthan) — a livestock fair, not a tourism festival.
